steps.message:
Define the palette once and apply the pairs through implicit styles in App.xaml:

```xml
<Application.Resources>
    <ResourceDictionary>
        <Color x:Key="LightPageBackground">#FFFFFF</Color>
        <Color x:Key="DarkPageBackground">#1E1E1E</Color>
        <Color x:Key="LightPrimaryText">#222222</Color>
        <Color x:Key="DarkPrimaryText">#F2F2F2</Color>

        <Style TargetType="ContentPage"
               ApplyToDerivedTypes="True">
            <Setter Property="BackgroundColor"
                    Value="{AppThemeBinding
                        Light={StaticResource LightPageBackground},
                        Dark={StaticResource DarkPageBackground}}" />
        </Style>

        <Style TargetType="Label">
            <Setter Property="TextColor"
                    Value="{AppThemeBinding
                        Light={StaticResource LightPrimaryText},
                        Dark={StaticResource DarkPrimaryText}}" />
        </Style>
    </ResourceDictionary>
</Application.Resources>
```

Pages and labels now inherit system light/dark colors without repeating literals. For a one-off code-built control:

```csharp
var label = new Label { Text = "Status" };
label.SetAppThemeColor(
    Label.TextColorProperty,
    Colors.DarkGreen,
    Colors.LightGreen);
label.SetAppTheme<double>(
    Label.FontSizeProperty,
    14,
    16);
```

SetAppThemeColor is the color-specific helper; SetAppTheme<T> handles other bindable property types.
